item.title: Apec summit live: Xi and Putin start talks; Rubio says Trump serious about meeting Kim Jong-un
item.description:
Summit in Chinese tech hub Shenzhen set to include highly anticipated meeting between Xi, Trump and Putin

  • Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit

  • What is Apec? Explained in 30 seconds

Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up?

That is the question the Guardian’s diplomatic correspondent Patrick Wintour seeks to address in his piece about the expected, Putin, Trump and Xi, meeting at Apec on Thursday.

It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse.

item.description:
Iran's army launches drone attack at Kuwait base used by US military

Iran’s army has said it fired a drone targeting the Ali al-Salem Airbase in Kuwait, according to Iranian state media IRNA.

"This morning, the Islamic Republic of Iran's army's destructive combat drones targeted Patriot defense systems and drone and missile launchers of the US terrorist army at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait with destructive drones," the statement read.

"In defense of Iran, we will not bow to any power, but our response to any threat or aggression will be decisive, crushing, and without geographical limitations," the army added

item.title: Australian wages grow at fastest pace since 2023 – but prices are climbing even more quickly
item.description:
Wage rates climb about 1 percentage point faster than before pandemic, triggering warnings of a sixth RBA rate rise

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Wages grew at their fastest pace since late 2023 over the three months to September, buoyed up by this year’s boost to minimum pay rates for millions of lower paid workers – but still not fast enough to keep up with the rising cost of living.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ wage price index climbed by 1.1% in the most recent quarter, lifting the annual increase to 3.5% – a pace that economists said would keep the Reserve Bank on edge about the need for further interest rate hikes.

item.title: US Centcom commander expected in Saudi Arabia with dozens of air defence experts, sources say
item.description:
US Centcom commander expected in Saudi Arabia with dozens of air defence experts, sources say

US Central Command chief admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of forces in the Middle East, is expected to arrive in Saudi Arabia this week with advisors to examine the kingdom’s air defence capabilities, multiple western officials familiar with the matter told Middle East Eye.

The officials, speaking to MEE on condition of anonymity, said more than three dozen US military advisors are going to Saudi Arabia to help the kingdom with its air defence. Some have already started arriving, the officials said.

The visit comes as the kingdom reels from Houthi aerial attacks amid a sensitive time in US-Saudi relations.

item.title: Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran
item.description:
Rubio says 'no imminent threat' to US from Iran

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cast doubt about reports of an "imminent threat" from Iran on Washington.

Speaking to reporters in the Philippines, Rubio said that US authorities routinely check for  potential threats against the country, but added that most intelligence leads are not considered credible. 

When asked if he was concerned about a possible attack on Washington, he said: "I am not. But again, we're concerned every day about anything that threatens our country ... I don't think there's any imminent threat."

"The United States is always on the lookout for anyone who tries to do harm to our country and to our people. And we have threat streams every day, and the majority of them are not credible. We have to follow up on them," Rubio added.

Rubio also questioned the credibility of sources cited in a CNN report about an alleged Iranian plot targeting the US capital, saying: "Some of your intelligence sources are liars; others are liars and criminals."

"I won't even comment on it because I don't know who's leaking this stuff to you guys. But they're either showboats and liars, or probably criminals if they're saying anything that's even half true."

item.title: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
item.description:
With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea

At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.

Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.
